newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal -Values mostly flat, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal -Values mostly flat, trade quiet.

text.p: Soymeal basis offers were mostly unchanged on Thursday in quiet trade, cash dealers said.
"It's really quiet here, there's not a thing moving," said one Illinois dealer.
Some locations are beginning to quote prices over July CBOT futures, and most others expect to quote July by Friday or Monday, just before CBOT May soymeal expires on Tuesday.
"I'm seeing people go over to the July now and they're not taking as much of the spread as they thought they would be," said a dealer in the southeast.
Soymeal brokers have been offering spot soymeal over May futures in order to capture the significant premium that May holds to July.
Some dealers reported supplies were growing heavy in the south, and said there were several processors who had meal on track waiting for buyers.
Traders expect the National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush pace to fall within a range of 23.6 to 25.1 million bushels.
That figure compares with last week's crush of 24.6 million bushels, according to NOPA data.
